name: Kaplan Preference Matrix
citation: Kaplan, R. & Kaplan, S. (1989). The experience of nature: A psychological perspective. Cambridge University Press.

constructs.description: Low aggregate PE → fluency → preference. Maps to visual statistics + rapid gist + processing fluency.
Moderate PE → engagement on inverted-U. Maps to visual rhythm + novelty dopamine.
Low spatial PE → confident cognitive mapping. Maps to spatial integration + landmarks.
Anticipated PE reduction → dopaminergic wanting. Promenade sequencing + novelty anticipation + isovist control + safety gate.

schema_gaps: Semantic coherence not fully captured by visual statistics alone
irreducible_residual.narrative: The Kaplan Matrix may BE Predictive Processing applied to environmental scenes. Each variable maps to a specific region of the PE landscape — Coherence to fluency zone, Complexity to engagement zone, Legibility to spatial confidence zone, Mystery to anticipated-PE-reduction reward zone. The irreducible residuals — semantic coherence, expertise-dependent optima, mystery-danger interaction — all require IE-DPT.

key_references: Kaplan, R. & Kaplan, S. (1989). The experience of nature. Cambridge University Press.
Kaplan, S. (1987). Aesthetics, affect, and cognition. Environ. Behav., 19(1), 3-32.

variables.Mystery: Promise of information if one goes deeper (inferred exploration)

predictions: Mystery strongest single predictor of preference (r ≈ 0.35)
Coherence and complexity jointly predict 40-55% of landscape preference

provenance.seminal_paper: Kaplan, R. & Kaplan, S. (1989). The experience of nature: A psychological perspective. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
provenance.earlier_formulation: Kaplan, S., Kaplan, R., & Brown, T. (1989). Environmental preference: A comparison of four domains of predictors. Journal of Environmental Psychology, 9(3), 215-226. doi:10.1016/s0272-4944(89)80001-1
provenance.predecessor: Berlyne's optimal arousal theory (1971); preference rating methodology from environmental psychology; landscape architecture preference studies
provenance.historical_context: Rachel and Stephen Kaplan began research on nature-psychology relationships in the 1970s at University of Michigan. Developed the four-variable model of environmental preference: Coherence (immediate understanding), Complexity (immediate exploration interest), Legibility (inferred understanding/navigability), and Mystery (inferred exploration/information promise). Model operationalized environmental preference as integration of immediate and inferred psychological responses.
key_milestones: 1970s: Rachel & Kaplan's initial research on nature preferences
1987: Kaplan's foundational work on aesthetics, affect, and cognition (Environment & Behavior)
1989: Publication of The Experience of Nature (comprehensive framework)
1989: Environmental Preference paper with Brown empirically validating four-variable model
1990s-2000s: Development of Attention Restoration Theory (ART) as complement
2000s-Present: Application to landscape architecture, environmental design, and restoration ecology
influenced_by: Rachel Kaplan (environmental psychologist, U of Michigan)
Stephen Kaplan (psychologist, cognitive science, U of Michigan)
Terry Brown (empirical validation and cross-domain testing)
Environmental psychology tradition of preference rating studies
provenance.current_status: foundational and widely applied; active research in landscape architecture, environmental design, and restoration
provenance.verification_notes: Seminal work (1989) verified via Cambridge University Press. Kaplan, Kaplan & Brown (1989) empirical paper verified via Journal of Environmental Psychology. Both publication dates confirmed (1987 Kaplan aesthetics paper, 1989 comprehensive works). Google Scholar citation count confirmed at 5,000+. Model's four variables (coherence, complexity, legibility, mystery) verified across multiple design and landscape psychology sources.
